decisions.reason: The rye country bread fits the core range and runs on existing production, so it costs little to keep, and with no negative signal there is no reason to abandon it yet.
The repeatedly gold-medalled flagship stollen has shown realized value and deserves continued commitment, more so now that the marzipan variant has been withdrawn.
The seeded rye mixed bread is a cheap variant of established recipes, and with no evidence of weak demand the option stays open.

The dark malt rye bread overlaps with the other rye products, which makes it the most likely candidate for pruning, but its low upkeep cost and lack of negative results justify keeping it another year.
The ancient grain 'masterpiece' is still recent and promoted as a highlight, so its uncertain upside is worth preserving at low cost.
